title: fix: recover oversized reply attachments through Files
body: ## What Problem This Solves When an assistant saves a file successfully but its reply attachment exceeds the existing delivery limit, the chat can show a generic delivery failure and suggest trying again. The unchanged file will fail again, even when the user can already access the saved output through Files. The failure also loses the distinction between a size refusal and a transient delivery problem. ## User Impact Oversized reply attachments get a native attachment card with the filename, the message “Too large to attach. Look for this file in Files.”, and a **Find in Files** action when the current chat supports it. The action opens the existing Files browser with a filename search. Users deliberately select a result, inspect its location, and use the existing preview or download action. A filename is a search aid; it is never treated as proof of a file's identity or location. The action preserves open previews and unsaved drafts and is withheld for attachments attributed to another session or agent. Existing access checks still decide whether a file can be listed or read, including after permissions change. Size limits, file formats, saved bytes, and successful small attachments are unchanged. Older text clients retain a visible warning through the existing display-text fallback. ## Why This Change Was Made The media loaders did not consistently preserve typed size failures: the local byte-limit path threw a generic error, and the remote reader failed before returning enough information for the host to classify the refusal. The existing reply preparation owner now recognizes the existing typed size errors and emits a distinct attachment failure. An oversized remote file returns bounded metadata without reading its body; the host validates that response and issues the typed refusal. The existing finalization function shares the unoptimized image/document byte check and result construction, preserving image-specific limits and dimension validation without adding another layer. The SSH workspace reader also preserves its actual bounded-read error without parsing diagnostic text. Older-client text fallback is projected by the Gateway, keeping server reply metadata out of the browser startup graph. The Control UI uses the size distinction to offer the existing Files search instead of an identical retry. Search stays with the current session's Files owner, which checks the captured connection and workspace identity before loading results. Recovery does not add a download endpoint, a persistent file locator, or an access grant. The documentation describes the search and explicit selection step. ## Evidence A native assistant produced a valid ZIP above the effective 5 MiB reply limit and a small sample ZIP. Before this change, the large attachment showed a generic failure while Files could download the original ZIP intact; the small sample delivered normally. A separate isolated reproduction traced the local failure through the byte-limit check and exercised the real remote workspace reader. Changed-file formatting, lint, the UI catalog check, selected compiler graphs, and the test-line check passed. The 302 selected test files produced 301 passing file entries and 5,679 passing assertions; one platform-specific file and five tests were skipped. After simplifying the media finalization owner, its 29 related files were rerun: 529 assertions passed, with the same platform skip; unaffected earlier results remain applicable. The three regression cases fail on the original owners and pass with this change: typed remote rejection, real ZIP delivery with a healthy small-file control, and the unchanged text-client reader. UI tests cover the action, session attribution, stale connections, preserved drafts, ambiguous results, and deliberate file selection. The aggregate test command retains one inherited failure: the uncaught Node 24.22.1 / Undici 7.30.1 data-URL abort error tracked in #188084. The unchanged attachment test reproduces the same error on the exact base and this candidate, with all 30 assertions passing in each run. Its fetch and cleanup owners are unchanged. No assertion or cleanup was suppressed, and this PR does not claim to fix that runtime error. The first hosted build identified a startup regression: chat boot required 23 JavaScript requests versus 20 on the matched base. Moving the compatibility projection to the Gateway removes the extra browser imports. The corrected candidate passes `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 6fdd9aaf60cd92cdc967016ff419a029bbe716a3`: 20 chat boot requests, 1,272,942 gzip bytes, and every existing startup, JavaScript-byte and CSS budget intact. The native pair uses the declared Vite 8.3.4 toolchain; hosted CI also passes with its merged Vite 8.3.5 toolchain. This is a deterministic build comparison, not a latency claim. Independent review identified an additional SSH source-limit path. The real pinned Python reader and reply normalizer reproduced the generic failure at 25,165,825 bytes against a 25,165,824-byte source cap; the corrected path produces the size-specific warning while the small ZIP still delivers. The strengthened existing reader test fails on the original owners and passes on the correction. The correction batch passed 1,268 assertions across 63 executed test files, with 17 native skips; an opt-in live cron consumer was not run because its imported predicate and provider behavior are unchanged. SSH transport is source-qualified; this is not a newly executed SSH-network/model turn. A real guest on the current head used the keyboard to open **Find in Files**, selected `exports/orders-large.zip`, and downloaded 8,874,168 bytes matching the saved ZIP's SHA-256. The ZIP contains 80,000 unique rows; the healthy sample matches its saved source. Desktop and 400px captures show the native card. The unsent chat draft survived recovery, and a separate native editor flow retained an unsaved file draft without changing the saved file. Independent review closed the SSH finding; its current-head recheck and the required automated review are clean. Hosted CI is green. One streaming shard initially observed four commits where it expected zero. A matched native replay reproduced that assertion on the actual CI base while the actual merge candidate passed all six cases; the single unchanged hosted shard revalidation passed. No assertion, budget or implementation was changed to obtain that result, and this PR does not claim to repair the unrelated streaming failure. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Desktop native card crops, 656px wide; native card crops aligned on an unscaled transparent canvas | ![Retained original failure on current baseline UI; no recovery action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e71b57ed-02cd-4d26-a3fa-4595ecd8b8cb) | ![Narrow attachment card wraps guidance and preserves the recovery action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f3983d2-389a-495f-b051-fd1410958322) | ### Keyboard recovery through native Files, with exact\-byte download verification https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/519b6492-a026-4203-adee-1248b56e3706 ### Visual verification - Baseline: Original native failure before implementation; mobile retained failure rendered on ae01f1c113826d3ff41463e74da6c115e5b581ff - Exact head: `a797ce451ff575949928e47cde9443840d905f5f` - Scenario: Use the attachment card with the keyboard, search the current session, deliberately select exports/orders\-large\.zip and download the unchanged saved ZIP\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.9\-a797ce451ff5\-2026\-10\-31T03\-52\-00\.434Z; native source\-backed Control UI - Recovered ZIP: 8,874,168 bytes; SHA\-256 matches the saved source - Current\-head interaction: Tab and Enter open filename search; explicit path selection precedes download - Drafts: Unsent chat draft and independently exercised unsaved editor draft are retained - Actual guest session and real assistant\-generated ZIP on the exact published head - Existing access checks and deliberate result selection remain in use - Desktop and narrow card captures use native pixels; only transparent framing is added - Recording has a measured initial zoom, factual captions and an unrelated bottom\-controls redaction - SSH size refusal separately proven at the real bounded\-reader owner; unchanged SSH network transport is source\-qualified, not newly executed
